checkers.substitution: No submission can put a filter on the graded readout, because the harness owns the readout and computes it from its own trained parameters. The rejecting half is carried on a planted telemetry fixture and the substitution is recorded in tests/checkers.yaml.
A submission never runs inside the grading process, so it cannot substitute the parameter snapshot that is evaluated. The rejecting half is carried on a planted telemetry fixture.

A dip wide enough to break the band cannot be produced on demand by a spec, because the readings are the harness's own and move smoothly in the flat tail of the training curve. The rejecting half is carried on a planted telemetry fixture that widens one point.

grade.py consumes a fixed key list that never includes a submission field, so no submission can add itself to it. The rejecting half is carried on a planted fixture that adds a submission-owned key to the consumed list.

checkers.discovery_value_note: `corpus.offset` is established ONLY in the built verifier image: it is the token position in the staged FineWeb validation shard at which the held-out slice opens, so it is readable off the staged shard bytes and appears in no agent-visible byte at all. The probe isolates it exactly: it hashes the raw token bytes it finds at that position and reports the position only when the digest is the pinned one, holding the period fixed, so the outcome is a function of the offset alone. A grading path pointed at any other slice cannot produce that position, and the checker's outcome moves the moment the phase moves.
checkers.substitution: No submission can move the phase of the held-out slice, because the slice is absent from the agent surface entirely and the harness reads it back off disk inside the verifier process. The rejecting half is carried on a fixture that perturbs the frozen construction phase this checker derives its expectation from, so the accepting half is the grounding-derived phase and the rejecting half is a wrong one.

checkers.discovery_value_note: `corpus.stride` is established ONLY in the built verifier image: it is the token count the held-out slice spans, so it is readable off the staged shard bytes and appears in no agent-visible byte. The probe isolates it exactly: it reports how many tokens the shard actually yielded at that position, which is a property of what the shard carried and not of where the read started, so the offset cancels identically and a shard too short to carry the period is refused rather than silently truncated.
checkers.substitution: No submission can move the period of the held-out slice, for the same reason. The rejecting half is carried on a fixture that perturbs the frozen construction stride this checker derives its expectation from, so the accepting half is the grounding-derived stride and the rejecting half is a wrong one.

statement_ambiguity.how_checked: adequacy.py drives both readings as two independent computations over the same reference telemetry and asserts the two floats are bit-identical, so the instruction admits one reading of what is optimized rather than two that happen to agree in the reference case.
